tasks.registered_metrics_text:
a) Define the metric(s) to assess a property of an algorithm. These metrics should reflect the desired algorithm
properties described in assessment aim(s) (see above). State which metric(s) were used to compute the ranking(s) (if
any).
  • Example 1: Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC)
  • Example 2: Area under curve (AUC)
Several metrics will be used to determine the ranking of the challenge, given two volumes A
and B:


Dice per case:
DICE(A,B) = (2|A intersection B|)/|A|+|B|)


Average Symmetric Surface Distance (ASD):


ASD(A,B) = (1/(|S(A)|+|S(B)|))
* [sum_{s_A in S(A)} d(s_A, S(B)) + sum_{s_B in S(B))} d(s_B, s(A))]


with d(v,s) = min_{s_A in S(A)} ||v-s_A|| and S(A) the set of surface voxels of A;


5 mm Surface Dice (SD):


SD(A,B) = (card_5(A,B) + card_5(B,A)) with card_5(A,B) = card({s_A in S(A)/d(s_A, S(B)) < 5mm}) and card (X) the
cardinal of the set X .


Maximum Symmetric Surface Distance (MSD):




 A tumor and liver automatic segmentation challenge

MSD(A,B) = max{max_{s_A in S(A)} d(s_A, S(B)), max_{s_B in S(B)} d(s_B, S(A)}


Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) on tumor burden estimation on the whole dataset:


RMSE = sqrt[1/n * sum_{i=1}^n (Tb_Ai - Tb_Bi)^2]


with n the number of images and TbAi and TbBi the tumor burden of the ground truth and
the prediction of the ith image, respectively. The tumor burden is defined as follows:


Tb = VT / (VL + VT)


with VL the volume of healthy liver and VT the volume of the tumor.


For DICE, SD, ASD and MSD, the average value over the test dataset will be calculated. Each metric, except the
RMSE on tumor burden estimation, will be calculated twice. The first time on the liver segmentation and the
second time on the tumor segmentation. If for a given
metric there is an equality between two models, we favor the one with the lowest standard
deviation (if calculable) on the test dataset.

b) Justify why the metric(s) was/were chosen, preferably with reference to the biomedical application.

Geometrical metrics are combined with volume estimations to link computer vision
accuracy and clinical implications.


Dice scores are measures focusing on the overlap between two volumes. Those metrics allow to measure the
similarity between the ground truth and the prediction of a model
(per image for the dice per case and on the whole test dataset for the global dice). The SD tolerates errors close to
the ground truth but will penalize errors far from the ground truths
such as missed secondary lesions, providing insights on such cases.


ASD and MSD are surface distance metrics providing information related to the maximum
and average distances between the ground truth and prediction. Since HCC can take heterogenous forms, we are
looking for robust algorithms performing well on complicated
cases. Metrics such as MSD seem perfectly suited to measure the performance on these cases.


Finally, the tumor burden measurement provides information on the fraction of the liver
affected by cancer.
tasks.registered_ranking_text:
a) Describe the method used to compute a performance rank for all submitted algorithms based on the generated
metric results on the test cases. Typically the text will describe how results obtained per case and metric are aggregated
to arrive at a final score/ranking.

Rank-then-aggregate voting system will be used over the different metrics. The winning
submission will be the one with the best average ranking over all metrics.

b) Describe the method(s) used to manage submissions with missing results on test cases.



 A tumor and liver automatic segmentation challenge

Missing predictions will have the worst score on all metrics.

c) Justify why the described ranking scheme(s) was/were used.

All of the proposed metrics are complementary, supporting the idea that a method that
performs well overall is the most likely to find a clinical use.

registered_task_submissions.protocol_description: This challenge will take place before the conference. The participants are invited to submit their results through the dedicated website by uploading a docker container taking NIfTI images as input and providing as output the associated segmentation in NIfTI format. The evaluation metrics will be calculated automatically by the organizing team on the test dataset using the output NIfTI segmentation from the docker container and the ground truth images. The source code of the algorithm will not be directly requested. The submission will be done using docker as long as the website is open. Also, to be sure that we can handle every architecture, dockers will need to be configured to perform inference on cpu.
